Command: No Millstone Taken as a Pledge
Summary: No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge: for he taketh a man's life to pledge. This is the pledge law's hardest case, drafted separately from the entry-and-return rules that follow it.
Commandment: No one shall take the upper or nether millstone as a pledge.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as civil. The millstone was not ordinary collateral: it was the tool by which a household made its daily bread. Taking it was taking life itself, which is why Scripture says so in those words. The procedure belongs to Israel's civil law, but the principle — never secure a debt by taking what a person needs to live — is the mercy the New Testament still expects (James 2:15-16).
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: for he taketh a man's life to pledge (Deuteronomy 24:6).
